name: Karl Hermann Frank
role: Sudeten German Nazi politician; SS and police leader and German state minister in occupied Bohemia and Moravia
summary: Frank advocated German rule over Czech territory and racial Germanization through selective assimilation, expulsions and settlement. His occupation policy combined centralized authority, suppression of Czech cultural institutions and violent repression.

decide-locally.rationale: He explicitly praises centralized Reich authority over Czech territory, responsible only to Hitler.

right-to-secede.rationale: He rejects independent Czech statehood and insists on permanent inclusion within Germany.

political-violence-never.rationale: He ordered Lidice’s destruction and collective reprisals against its civilian inhabitants.

ethnic-nation.rationale: He explicitly makes complete Germanization of territory and inhabitants the goal.

territorial-expansion.rationale: He celebrates annexations as restoring German power and securing eastern living space.

national-self-determination.rationale: He expressly denies that Czech geography permits independent political statehood.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: His Germanization program makes marriage conditional on prior racial examination.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: He sorts Czechs by racial suitability, prescribing expulsion or killing for rejected groups.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Inferred: his compulsory assimilation and expulsions subordinate inhabitants to Germanization regardless of their wishes.

population-transfer.rationale: His memorandum prescribes expelling Czechs deemed racially unsuitable or politically hostile.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: His ordered destruction of Lidice punished civilians without evidence connecting them to the assassination.

separated-powers.rationale: Inferred: his proposed single authority controls planning and execution, subordinate directly to Hitler.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: After the Heydrich attack he personally imposed martial law and launched repression.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: He depicts Slavic civilization as determined by Germanic cultural preponderance.

minority-language-support.rationale: He proposes abolishing Czech schools and eliminating Czech as an official language.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: He endorses incorporating Sudeten German territory into the German Reich.

patriotic-education.rationale: He demands education in Reich ideology and eradication of Czech historical identity.

former-empire-influence.rationale: He urges renewed German political control in the former imperial Bohemian heartland.

single-official-language.rationale: He demands German proficiency while reducing Czech to an unofficial dialect.

majority-settlement.rationale: He proposes German settlements and connecting corridors extending toward Prague.

historical-land-claim.rationale: His lecture invokes ancient German rule to justify permanent control over Czech lands.

suppress-opposition.rationale: He prescribes severe policing, exile and lethal special treatment for political opponents.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: He praises Hitler’s intervention and annexation as liberation of Sudeten Germans.

notes: The 1940 memorandum and 1941 lecture establish his own policy, separately from Hans Frank and from Neurath. Historical deductions are marked Inferred. His tactical resistance to Hitler’s proposed killing of 10,000 Czechs does not cancel his own reprisals. No positions are assigned merely from Nazi membership, religious affiliation or attendance at meetings. Remaining statements were checked against the downloaded texts; specific economic systems, family and sexual laws, environmental policy and modern technologies lack individual evidence. Death-penalty doctrine and drug-specific extrajudicial killing remain null: collective civilian murder does not establish those particular formulations.
